text:
acme_frontend: Hey team — customer (Acme Payments) reporting intermittent SSE streams that stop mid-event. Happens behind Fastly and on Safari. Client shows partial 'data:' payload then connection closes. When client reconnects EventSource gets a 401 on the reconnect request. Repro steps below, logs attached. Any immediate fixes? cc @jess_support

jess_support: Thanks — can you paste the raw client console/network logs and server logs? Also, are you using the native EventSource or a polyfill? How are you attaching auth (header vs query vs cookie)?

acme_frontend: Native EventSource in most cases. We tried event-source-polyfill in one customer test. Auth is currently via short-lived bearer token in query string (e.g. /events?token=...); we couldn't use Authorization header because EventSource doesn't support custom headers. Logs:

Client console excerpt:
```
EventSource failed to connect: 401
EventSource received partial data: "{\"text\":\"...incomplete"
net::ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING
```

Server log around same time:
```
[sse] client connect token=eyJ.. ok
[sse] send chunk id=34 len=512
[sse] client disconnect id=34: connection reset by peer
[sse] reconnect attempt token=eyJ.. -> 401 invalid_token
```

Also noticed Fastly sometimes returns 304 for the SSE endpoint when the upstream returns 200 and we use conditional headers. Not sure how that interacts.

ben_infra: A few likely culprits, prioritized: token expiry on reconnect, CDN caching/304 interaction, and Safari-specific buffering behavior. Quick pointers:
- EventSource cannot set Authorization header; query-token or cookie are the typical ways.
- If you put token in query, ensure CDN doesn't cache or normalize the URL in a way that drops auth semantics. Configure Fastly to pass-through Authorization or treat the SSE path as non-cacheable.
- Set these response headers on the SSE endpoint: `Cache-Control: no-store, must-revalidate`, `Surrogate-Control: no-store`, and `Vary: Authorization` (if using header auth). Avoid 304s for SSE — 304 with no body will break streaming clients.

Minimal Node/Express SSE example we recommend (send these headers):
```
res.writeHead(200, {
  'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-store, must-revalidate',
  'Connection': 'keep-alive',
  'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': 'https://app.acme.com',
  'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials': 'true'
});
res.write('retry: 5000\\n\\n'); // suggested client retry
```

sam_engineer: Adding to ben — token expiry mid-stream is common. If the client reconnects and the token has expired you'll get 401s which then look like "disconnect on reconnect". Options:
- Use a rotating stream token that the client refreshes via a short websocket/fetch call and appends to reconnect URL.
- Issue a long-lived session cookie for the SSE domain (HttpOnly + Secure) so EventSource will send it automatically.
- Implement a graceful server resume using `Last-Event-ID` and accept a short-lived reconnect token to re-authorize and resume.

Also note: some CDNs and proxies (Fastly, CloudFront) will respond with 304 for conditional requests. For streaming endpoints that must never be cached you should strip ETag/If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since behavior at the CDN and set origin to `Cache-Control: no-store` so clients/proxies don't serve 304s.

maria_ce: Safari-specific: we've seen Safari (esp. <16) stall if the initial response is too small or if the connection is converted to a 304 by an intermediate cache. Workarounds that helped customers:
- Ensure the SSE origin writes an initial keep-alive comment / padding (e.g., `:\\n\\n` or `: ping\\n\\n`) to flush the connection.
- Avoid `Content-Length` and let transfer-encoding chunked be used.
- Disable caching for the route in CDN and on origin.

acme_frontend: Helpful — thanks. We can try cookie route but our customers are multi-tenant and we set tokens per workspace. Do you have a suggested quick repro we can give them to run locally?

sam_engineer: Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start a local server that serves SSE at `/sse?token=<token>` and enforces token expiry after 10s. Server will write a few events then sleep 2s then close.
2) Use native EventSource in Chrome and Safari with the query token. After ~12s the client will reconnect — if token expired server returns 401 on reconnect.
3) Simulate CDN by adding a reverse proxy that rewrites/strips `If-None-Match` and returns 304 on second request. Watch Safari stall.

Client snippet to reproduce (put in browser console):
```
const es = new EventSource('/sse?token=SHORT_LIVED');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('es error', e);
```

Polyfill fallback (XHR streaming) — useful for browsers where you need to add headers or tolerate 304s. Example idea (very simplified):
```
const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest();
xhr.open('GET', '/sse?token=SHORT_LIVED', true);
xhr.onreadystatechange = () => {
  if (xhr.status === 200 && xhr.responseText) {
    // parse incremental chunks from xhr.responseText
  }
};
xhr.send();
```
Note: polyfills allow custom headers but are heavier and have edge cases for chunk parsing.

ben_infra: Action items:
- @sam_engineer: add origin headers + padding + retry header on SSE endpoint and document cookie vs query token tradeoffs (ETA EOD).
- @jess_support: ask customer to enable Fastly debug logs for the failing requests and confirm whether Fastly is returning 304s for the SSE path.
- @acme_frontend: try `Cache-Control: no-store` on origin for the SSE route and confirm if Safari continues to stall. If still failing, give us a HAR and we'll escalate to infra.

deploy-bot: deploy reported: sse-fixes branch merged to staging at 2026-03-15T14:22:00Z — changes include `Cache-Control: no-store` and initial padding.

acme_frontend: Will test and report back. If this reproduces we can ask the customer to switch to cookie auth for the stream or to a short reconnect token refresh flow. Really appreciate the quick triage. :thanks:
